'''Engineering Materials''' are resources consumed when applying ship [[Engineering Blueprints|Engineering blueprints]] and [[Experimental Effects]]. They are stored in a dedicated inventory, do not use [[Cargo Rack|cargo space]], add no ship mass, and remain available when changing between ships, SRVs, and ship-launched fighters.<ref name="fandom-materials">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Materials Materials], Elite Dangerous Wiki, accessed 2026-09-15.</ref>

Ship Engineering materials are separate from the goods, assets, and data used for [[Odyssey Engineering|Odyssey suit and weapon Engineering]].

== Material types ==

{| class="wikitable"
! Type
! Grades
! Typical sources
|-
| '''Raw'''
| Grade 1–4
| Surface prospecting, asteroid mining by-products, missions, and certain material sites
|-
| '''Manufactured'''
| Grade 1–5
| Ship salvage, signal sources, missions, and other recovered components
|-
| '''Encoded'''
| Grade 1–5
| Ship and wake scans, data points, signal sources, missions, and other data collection
|}

A material's grade indicates its rarity and its position within its Material Trader family. Higher-grade Engineering blueprints normally require rarer materials, but the exact recipe belongs on the relevant blueprint page.

== Storage ==

Each material has its own storage limit. Collecting one material never displaces another.

|-

Raw materials end at Grade 4; manufactured and encoded materials extend to Grade 5.<ref name="fandom-materials" />

== Acquisition ==

Sources are material-specific. The broad type indicates where to begin searching, but the fastest reliable source for one material may be unsuitable for another. Mission boards can award materials from all three ship-Engineering inventories, while salvage and scans provide type-specific alternatives.

Update 18.08 increased material availability at Grade 4 and Grade 5 farming locations and raised Engineering-material mission rewards. Frontier documented mission rewards of up to 24 units depending on the mission, material, and difficulty.<ref name="frontier-1808">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/type-8-update-now-available Type-8 Update is Now Available], Frontier Developments, 7 August 2024, accessed 2026-09-15.</ref>

The current [[Tools and Resources#Engineering and material tracking|Engineering tools]] can identify required quantities and help locate material sources before a gathering trip. Individual material articles own material-specific acquisition information; complete gathering routes belong in dedicated procedures.

== Material Traders ==

Material Traders exchange materials within one inventory type: Raw, Manufactured, or Encoded. They cannot exchange ship Engineering materials for Odyssey goods, assets, or data.

Trades are lossy. Exchanging a rarer material downward in the same family yields more units; trading upward or across families costs progressively more. This makes traders useful for converting a surplus, but collecting the required material directly is normally more efficient than repeatedly trading across families.

Station services identify which trader type is present. Community databases such as Inara provide current material listings and station-service searches.<ref name="inara-components">[https://inara.cz/elite/components Components], Inara, accessed 2026-09-15.</ref>

== EDFM material references ==

EDFM currently has dedicated references for:

* [[Classified Scan Databanks]] — Grade 5 encoded material;
* [[Electrical Wiring]] — Odyssey technology asset;
* [[Weapon Component]] — Odyssey technology asset.

Use [[:Category:Engineering Materials]] to browse the material pages currently available. The Odyssey entries are labelled separately because they do not belong to the Raw, Manufactured, or Encoded ship-material inventories.
